@raydalio #05 366,000 views
Almost every technology boom creates a bubble, then a bust, whether it’s railroads, the Industrial Revolution, or the late 1920s. Think about the late ‘20s: electricity, refrigeration, telephones, radios, airplanes, and cars were all emerging at once. Naturally, people wanted to invest in these miracles. The danger is that people fail to distinguish the miracle from the investment. A technology can be truly transformative, but if the stocks are priced too high or bought on debt, you get a crash. That is the mechanics behind how bubbles form and burst. New technology will be great, there is no doubt about that, but we always have to ask: great for whom, does it pay, and are we paying too much for the miracle? It was great discussing this and other topics with Masterclass CEO David Rogier and future members of the @masterclass Executive program. You can learn more about the program using the link in my bio. #Investing #Economy #EconomicCycles #Markets

@socho.abhi #07 97,100 views
Comment “SUGAR” for the report with sources. Sugar in India sits at the intersection of food inflation, farmer incomes, mill economics, ethanol policy, cooperative finance and political power. The government-set minimum selling price for sugar has remained ₹31/kg since February 2019, even as the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane has kept rising and is now ₹365/quintal for 2026–27. As of April, nearly ₹13,000 crore of cane dues for the current season were still unpaid. In Maharashtra, this gets even more complicated. Peer-reviewed economic research has found that politically controlled sugar mills can behave differently around elections, including paying farmers lower cane prices in election years. Before Maharashtra’s 2024 election, at least 61 candidates reportedly had links to sugar mills; 35 won. And underneath all of those policy debates is the labour actually harvesting the cane. A Maharashtra government inquiry found that 13,861 of 82,309 surveyed women sugarcane cutters in Beed — nearly 17% — had undergone hysterectomies. Separate research in parts of Beed found rates as high as 36%, versus roughly 3% nationally, amid documented pressure created by punishing work conditions, lost wages, debt and lack of menstrual sanitation. So no, the explanation is not simply “ethanol took all our sugar.” Ethanol matters. Weather matters. Forecasting errors matter. Prices and policy matter. Politics matters. Labour conditions matter. Six headlines that look unrelated are actually different layers of the same commodity. Sit facing the weight stack and secure your thighs firmly under the pads. 2. Grip the bar with a closed, pronated grip (palms facing forward), slightly wider than shoulder-width. 3. Keep your feet firmly on the floor, torso slightly leaned back, and spine neutral. 4. Extend your arms fully and maintain a stable position throughout the movement. ▶ DOWNWARD MOVEMENT 5. Pull the bar down toward the upper chest while driving the elbows down and slightly backward. 6. Keep the chest lifted and torso stable. Avoid swinging or leaning backward excessively. 7. Bring the bar toward the upper chest/clavicle area in a controlled manner. ▶ UPWARD MOVEMENT 8. Slowly return the bar to the starting position under control. 9. Allow the elbows to fully extend without letting the weight pull your arms up suddenly. 10. Maintain the same torso position throughout the movement. 📚 Source: National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) #latpulldown #backworkout #fitnessjourney

The wild part is that this isn’t a living fly brain uploaded into a computer. It’s a simulation built from its biological wiring map, showing how quickly an open neuroscience dataset can turn into experiments nobody expected. Sauna post-resistance training may enhance muscle growth. I just finished resistance training, and now I’m in the sauna. What interests me is whether heat can do more than help recovery but whether it can influence how our muscles adapt to training. A new meta-analysis from Dr. Brad Schoenfeld (@bradschoenfeldphd) and colleagues combined six studies involving 125 people. It found a small, possible advantage for muscle growth when heat was applied after lifting but no clear additional strength benefit. The studies had limitations, so this is encouraging, not conclusive. Heat is itself a cellular stressor. Human muscle-biopsy research has shown that adding whole-body heat after resistance exercise can increase heat-shock protein expression and activate mTOR signaling, part of the machinery that regulates muscle protein synthesis. That provides a plausible mechanism. My protocol is about 20 minutes in a hot sauna at 180 F after lifting, because I’m interested not just in potential muscle adaptations, but in long-term cardiovascular and brain health. In Finnish men followed for about 20 years, sauna use 4-7 times per week was associated with 40% lower all-cause mortality, 50% lower cardiovascular mortality, and 66% lower dementia risk.

95% of gyms don’t have this machine The tibialis anterior is the muscle at the front of your lower leg, and you can train it without a machine. Tib Raise Target muscle: Tibialis Anterior Starting Position: 1. Attach a long resistance band to the side of a squat rack, with both ends facing toward you. 2. Sit on the floor with a foam roller under your calves. Place the band around both feet at the laces. 3. Move slightly backward to create enough tension in the band. How to Perform: 4. Pull your toes up toward your shins against the band’s resistance (ankle dorsiflexion). 5. Slowly return to the starting position. Tip: You can also perform this exercise on a bench using a dumbbell between your feet. Keep your calves hanging off the edge of the bench and parallel to the floor, then perform the same movement. 📚 Source: National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) #tibialisanterior #calfraises #fitness

He Paid ₹41 Lakh for a ₹13 Lakh Land Purchase A US-based NRI got hit with a penalty of around ₹41 lakh. Not for a scam. Not for hiding money. But for buying a property in India. NRIs can buy properties of any form, except agricultural land, plantation property, or farmhouses. FEMA draws a hard line around these. An NRI cannot buy them. They can’t even receive it as a gift, even from parents. The only legal way to own it is inheritance. This is exactly where that US citizen got it wrong. He bought agricultural property in Tamil Nadu for ₹13.68 lakh, without getting the prior RBI approval the law requires. The original penalty calculated came close to ₹1.5 crore a base amount plus a share of the gain he made. FEMA caps penalties at three times the contravention amount, so it was brought down. He still ended up paying around ₹41 lakh, on a ₹13.68 lakh purchase. If you’re buying land anywhere near a farm, plantation, or countryside plot, stop and check before you sign anything. Are you sure that “countryside plot” you’re eyeing isn’t classified as agricultural land? #FEMA #NRIProperty #AgriculturalLand #NRIIndia #PropertyLaw RBI NRIFinance

One is that it’s essential and establishes the opportunity to make much more income later in life (as well as intellectual enrichment). The other is that it’s a waste of money generates a lot of loans and doesn’t teach practical skills; aka a waste of time. Obviously, some depends on what career people are interested in. For instance, you can’t be a doctor without training in biology, chemistry etc and doing a residency and internship, and you can’t be a research scientist and run a lab without formal training in your field of research and a PhD, and you can’t be a lawyer without going to law school in passing the bar exam. But there are valid points in arguments. My guest on the podcast is Joe Liemandt, the principal of Alpha school, where kids spend two hours a day learning cognitive skills and the rest of the time learning practical skills. Their performance on standardized tests, but also in life are astounding, so clearly they’re onto something. Here Joe shares their new approach to teaching kids financial literacy and learning how to start and run a business- very early. Before you say “Alpha school is only for rich kids” please note that they have started a scholarship program and overall, what they’re learning about education is intended to be applied more broadly in public schools going forward. I have no relationship to Alpha school financially or otherwise but I’m intrigued by what can allow learning to be more effective at all ages. The episode shares a lot of useful information that anyone can apply to learning anything. For kids and for adult adults. You can find the episode by going to hubermanlab.com. Finland is giving Study Visas to Indians up to the age of 50... And people are applying for Masters’ programs, where they can also take their family members and dependents along, and the dependants can also work in Finland while the primary members studies... In fact, the number of students in Finland Masters’ programs have almost doubled in 4 years... So Finland has a number of Masters’ programs taught in the English language across Computers, IT, AI, Data Sciences, Cybersecurity, Healthcare, Business, Engineering... and a lot more... Depending on the program you choose, the annual tuition fee is roughly EUR 12000 to 20000, which is lower than what one spends in the US and UK... and living expenses should be easily EUR 1200 per month... But look at the benefits: - You get an A Permit, which allows you to take up part time work of up to 30 hours per week, or 120 hours per month - Your family members and dependants can take up full time work to support themselves and the family - After your 2 years program, you also get an additional two years to extend in Finland, look for a job or to start a business - You can travel across the Schengen countries for 90 days out of 180 days - And there is no upper limit on when you want to enrol for a masters program If you wish to continue living in Finland though and find a job there after the program, it helps immensely to start learning Finnish on the side from the day you land so that you are ready to communicate till the end of your program. Also, you can’t fund your education only by your family members earning there, you have to show adequate savings to be able to fund your education and support your family... the working bit just helps you not erode all your savings away. #casarthakahuja

Why don’t we always train to failure? Research shows that a large portion of the hypertrophy and strength benefits can be achieved when a set is stopped within a few reps of failure, without the higher recovery cost and form breakdown associated with true failure. A range of 1–3 RIR can provide an effective stimulus while helping maintain training quality throughout the session. RIR can also help correct two common mistakes: Some people think every set should be taken to failure, while others always stop at 5+ RIR. RIR = Reps in Reserve It refers to the number of quality reps you could still perform when a set ends. For example, 2 RIR means that after finishing the set, you could still perform 2 clean reps. RIR has a direct relationship with RPE: RPE 8 ≈ 2 RIR RPE 9 ≈ 1 RIR RPE 10 = 0 RIR / Failure They’re essentially two ways of describing the same concept. RIR is often easier for athletes to understand because instead of asking them to rate intensity abstractly, it asks: “How many more reps could you have done?” RIR in the OPT Model Stabilization & Endurance: ~3–5 RIR Hypertrophy: mostly 1–3 RIR Strength: 1–3 RIR on heavy sets 0 RIR: only in rare, planned, and supervised situations RIR can also be used for weekly progression: Week 1 → 3 RIR Week 2 → 2 RIR Week 3 → 1 RIR Then → Deload Combined with the 2-for-2 rule for increasing weight, RIR can create a complete autoregulated progression system. 📚 Source: National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) #GymTok #gymfam #trainingtofailure #nycfitness

Taking Cash for Your Property Sale? Watch this first I almost made a huge mistake while selling my Bangalore flat last year. The buyer seemed serious, and said he wanted to pay 30 lakhs in cash. Honestly, for a moment, I considered it too. Registering the property at a lower value, and taking the rest in cash, can save on capital gains tax. But as an NRI, I can’t just sit on 30 lakhs in cash in India. If I deposit it in my bank account, income tax wants to know where it came from. If I give it to a family member to deposit, now they’re in trouble too. And taking it abroad is a completely different legal problem. Here’s what made me walk away completely. If the income tax department pulls this transaction for scrutiny and property deals above a certain value almost always get flagged both me and the buyer pay tax on the same 30 lakhs. He pays tax on it as unexplained income, at a rate far higher than any tax he’d have saved. I pay capital gains on the full actual sale value. We both lose more than we saved. I went back to the buyer and said: just to save 7% stamp duty, you’re going to pay 12.5% capital gains when you sell this flat later, calculated on an understated cost. We split the stamp duty difference and did the entire transaction through banking channels. If you’re an NRI selling property in India right now, has anyone suggested you take part of the payment in cash? #NRIProperty #CapitalGainsTax #NRIIndia #PropertySale #TaxPlanning BlackMoney NRIFinance

Elon Musk has predicted how the AI Bubble will burst soon... And to understand his argument, let’s unpack the three constraints that define AI in the world right now... 1/ Electricity Whenever you ask any question to a ChatGPT, Claude or any other model... the query is answered by semiconductor chips at a data centre that run a lot of computational data to give you the answer... and this requires a lot of power... Such that, right now the US is facing a structural problem with electricity... Where China currently generates more electricity than the US, Europe, and India combined... and in the past one year itself, it has added 40% of the entire US grid’s capacity of power... and created the whole US power grid’s capacity in just 4 years... So it is soon on a path to produce almost 4 times the electricity that the US produces in a year... that too with renewables, which are cheaper... Whereas in the US, the proposed new power plants are stuck such that they may take anywhere between 5-12 years to connect to the grid... So the US is about to lose very rapidly to China when it comes to the first constraint or raw material - electricity. 2/ Chips Right now, Nvidia makes the best chips in the world, but the US has put constraints on Nvidia shipping chips to China - where higher tariff would be imposed on chips being pushed to China because they are trying to starve China of access to chips... But quite like ASML makes the machines for creating chips, China has set up a company called SMIC which is already making chips 7 nm small... getting to 5 nm, and would soon reach a point where they can create their equally capable chips as well... 3/ AI Models China’s DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi K3 are already very good, and while being ranked in the top 5 models in the world, are already producing US model level output at 10% the cost... #casarthakahuja
